items.title: Who has jurisdiction over the flydubai incident?
items.summary: The aircraft left Dubai, was registered in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and was flying through Saudi Arabian airspace when the alleged confrontation took place before making an emergency landing in Tabuk. The aircraft also reportedly entered a rapid descent before passengers and crew intervened. This is where international aviation law becomes particularly important.

items.title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: F1 fans complain of gridlocked traffic, over three-hour waits for shuttles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Formula 1 spectators have complained of gridlocked roads, long shuttle bus queues and poor crowd management at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), after the first day of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia yesterday. Malaysian X user @tuakdotsol, said this morning that roads heading towards the circuit remained gridlocked, while private cars and e-hailing vehicles were apparently being stopped at the perimeter, funnelling spectators towards shuttle hubs at Mitsui Outlet Park and KLIA Terminal 2. “Apparently private cars and Grabs are blocked at the perimeter, so everyone funnels into shuttle hubs at Mitsui outlet and KLIA T2,” the user wrote, alongside images showing large crowds near the circuit.

items.title: Show decorum, respect Dr M's family privacy, Fahmi tells content creators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Content creators, influencers and social media users should prioritise decorum, consideration and humanity when generating content, particularly regarding the latest situation involving Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that while many were eager to know about the former prime minister's health status, not everything needed to be turned into news or social media content. Meanwhile, Fahmi reminded social media users not to spread speculative posts, insensitive artificial intelligence (AI)-generated material or inappropriate comments.

items.title: JB-Singapore RTS Link passenger service delayed to February
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link passenger service has been delayed to February, with final systems tests and trial runs expected to be completed by the end of this year. Singapore's RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO), the train service operator, said the revised timeline remained subject to independent safety certification and final regulatory approvals from Malaysia and Singapore. In a statement yesterday, RTSO said it expected to complete all systems tests and trial runs by Dec 31, followed by safety certification by an independent safety assessor.

items.title: 77-year-old man missing after car plunges into river
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: A 77-year-old man is missing after the car he was driving skidded into a river along Jalan Lubuk Segintah-Lubuk Kawah here early this morning. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said police received a call from a member of the public about 1am today informing them of an accident involving a car that had skidded into a river. He said preliminary investigations showed that Mat Yusof was driving from Jalan Kuala Ketil towards Teloi Timur Felda.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: 8,000 KL businesses renew licences in two months under streamlined system
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 3 — A total of 8,000 businesses in Kuala Lumpur renewed their business licences within two months after a new multi-year renewal initiative was introduced in July. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said 704 businesses opted for a two-year renewal, while 1,802 businesses renewed their licences for three years. For a two-year renewal, they receive a five per cent discount, which 704 businesses have opted for, while 1,802 businesses chose a three-year renewal to enjoy a 10 per cent discount on their business licence,” she said.

items.title: Malaysia’s largest MMEA vessel launched in Türkiye, set to sail home in January
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Construction of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency’s (MMEA) Multi-Purpose Mission Ship 1 (MPMS 1) is progressing smoothly and ahead of schedule, with the vessel expected to begin its voyage home in late January next year. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that upon completion and handover, MPMS 1 would make history as the largest vessel in the MMEA fleet. “I am in Istanbul, Türkiye today to witness the launch of MPMS 1, the MMEA’s new vessel being built at Desan Shipyard.

items.title: Bahrain F1 Grand Prix: Fans frustrated by hours-long waits for shuttle buses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Formula 1 (F1) fans have expressed frustration over the management of free shuttle bus services at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), with some claiming they had to wait for hours to board buses after leaving the venue yesterday. In a Threads post, a user identified as @dan_anyeal claimed he had queued for public transport about 5pm but only managed to board a bus four hours later. Four hours.

items.title: Husband and wife killed, two daughters seriously injured in Kluang crash
items.summary: Kluang police chief ACP Bahrin Mohd Noh said the crash involved a lorry driven by a 34-year-old man from Kluang heading towards Kahang and a Hyundai Matrix coming from the opposite direction. Bahrin said the lorry driver was not injured. Kluang Fire and Rescue Station commander Jusoh Mohd Salleh said they received an emergency call at 4.53pm.

items.title: #NSTViral: 'Even robots get nervous': Shaky android amuses Netizens [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A robot that appeared to suffer from "stage fright" has amused social media users after it was filmed shaking uncontrollably on stage at a government programme. View on Threads One Threads user joked: "I thought only humans got nervous on stage. Another user, n__aliahatiqah, wrote: "POV: after breastfeeding."

items.title: Motivational speaker under police investigation over alleged child sexual harassment in Perlis
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 3 — Police received a report on September 26 regarding an allegation of sexual harassment of a child by a motivational speaker. Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was lodged at 2.09am and the case is being investigated under Section 12 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. He urged other victims who may have had contact with the motivational speaker to come forward and lodge police reports.

items.title: Four areas in Sarawak and Johor record unhealthy API as haze persists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8.30am today, with Sri Aman, Sarawak recording the highest reading at 151. Sixty-one air quality monitoring stations recorded moderate API readings, while two stations recorded good API readings. No stations recorded API readings at very unhealthy or hazardous levels as of 8.30am today.

items.title: Oil tankers attacked in Hormuz strait: UK maritime agency
items.summary: TEHERAN: Two oil tankers have been struck by "unidentified projectiles" in the Strait of Hormuz region, a British maritime agency said Friday, in the latest threat to shipping in the waterway. The first attack caused "a small fire and blackout onboard", the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said Friday, adding that the fire was later extinguished. The agency said authorities were investigating the incidents.

items.title: Bahrain F1 Grand Prix: Visitors stuck for hours as congestion hits SIC, KLIA2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Visitors leaving the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after the first day of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 yesterday had to endure unusual traffic congestion. The congestion extended to Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2), where visitors were forced to queue for the Express Rail Link (ERL) to continue their journey home. Videos shared on social media showed queues of passengers filling the second floor of KLIA2, believed to include visitors making their way home after leaving SIC.

items.title: 'PJ MP's resignation another blow to PKR, but PH remains largely intact'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lee Chean Chung's resignation is another blow to PKR, with the party now struggling to retain even its own lawmakers. This, she said, showed that PKR was in "emergency mode". "This is really bad for PKR.

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile towards East Sea: Seoul
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile, Seoul's military said Saturday, a day after Pyongyang called the South "despicable" for demanding an apology over a blast in the demilitarised zone that wounded three of its soldiers. South Korea's military earlier this week demanded an official apology from the North. A day later, South Korea's dovish President Lee Jae Myung urged Pyongyang to return to dialogue.

items.title: Melaka election: Pas' willingness to use BN logo signals pragmatic approach
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas' willingness to contest the Melaka election under the Barisan Nasional logo shows that the latter now has stronger bargaining power, especially in the state. However, this is not simply a case of Pas "bowing" to BN, say analysts. Tawfik said the Registrar of Societies' suspension of Perikatan Nasional's activities had also prompted Pas to explore other options.

items.title: Budget 2027: Can Malaysia make its tax framework more M&A-friendly?
items.summary: Building a robust M&A tax framework is therefore necessary against this backdrop. Since the introduction of Capital Gains Tax (CGT) on unlisted local shares in 2024, the tax authorities have made a concerted effort to provide guidance to taxpayers navigating the new regime. For example, their confirmation that tax treaties which provide CGT relief would generally be respected on a self-assessment basis was well received.

items.title: Gold's US$4,100 slide may not mean cheaper gold for Malaysians [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The sharp correction in international gold prices may not translate into equally steep savings for Malaysian consumers, as the ringgit, type of gold product and seller spreads also determine local retail prices. Abdul Razak Gold House (M) Sdn Bhd managing director Mohd Razalie Abdul Rasul said the current decline reflected factors such as interest rates and oil prices. He reminded Malaysians that international gold prices did not directly determine retail prices.

items.title: China overtakes US as more positive influence in Latin America: Poll
items.summary: BOGOTÁ: China's influence in Latin America is now viewed more positively than that of the United States, a major poll conducted in 17 Latin American countries showed Friday. The 2026 Latinobarometro survey showed that China overtaking the United States in terms of influence for the first time since the annual survey began in 1995. It showed 57 per cent of people in Latin America considering the United States to be a positive influence, down from 60 per cent in 2020.

items.title: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels to ease global energy crunch
items.summary: PARIS: G7 countries agreed Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to ease global energy supply concerns, as President Donald Trump hailed the decision and said the US would not impose a threatened diesel export ban. They also said there would be no ban on diesel exports between them. Trump said European countries had agreed to release a "massive amount" of diesel from their reserves.

items.title: NST COURT WATCH: Taman Sri Muda floods, Zayn Rayyan appeal headline week in court [WATCH]
items.summary: One of the most significant rulings came from the Shah Alam High Court, which found the government liable for damages suffered by residents during the catastrophic 2021 floods in Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam. The court found the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) negligent, ruling that the local authority remained responsible for maintaining drains and related infrastructure within its jurisdiction. The court also held that MBSA was negligent.

items.title: NST CRIME WATCH: Bullying, rape, shooting and 'dirty dancing' [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Form Two student who died after allegedly being bullied at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah was beaten with a rubber hose by two senior students before he was found unconscious. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the two Form Four students were believed to have assaulted the victim after ordering him to retrieve the hose from a bathroom before taking him to two hostel rooms. The victim said she regained consciousness two hours later and found herself naked.

items.title: Bumper weekend in Malaysia: F1, football legends, concerts and comedy shows set to pack Klang Valley
items.summary: — AFP pic The biggest crowd-puller is the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, which got under way at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) yesterday and continues until tomorrow (October 4). Traffic diversions will be taking place on several roads leading to the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) from 8am to 11pm daily until October 4. Other affected roads include Jalan Raja, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Dang Wangi, Jalan Munshi Abdullah, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Kuching, Jalan Kinabalu and Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin.

items.title: How does cloud seeding work? What it could do for haze at Sepang this weekend
items.summary: The proposal comes as Malaysia has stepped up cloud seeding operations in response to the haze and hot, dry weather. What is cloud seeding? How does cloud seeding work?

items.title: Female US inmate on ventilator after botched lethal injection execution
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Convicted US murderer Christa Pike is unconscious on a ventilator after a botched attempt to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers said in a court filing Friday. As of Thursday evening, "Ms. Pike remains critically ill and is being treated at a Nashville-area hospital," lawyer Luke Ihnen wrote. - EXECUTION MORATORIUM - Pike's was the second failed execution in Tennessee this year.

items.title: US voices 'severe disappointment' over G20 trade talks deadlock
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US G20 presidency is "severely disappointed" that some members rejected a statement this week for action against excess industrial capacity, a criticism commonly aimed at China, according to a statement made public Friday. A draft ministerial statement against excess capacity, seen as driving costs down unfairly, "was supported by all but a handful of members," said top US trade official Jamieson Greer. Greer's chair statement, made public Friday, did not specify which countries disagreed.

items.title: Trump rules out US diesel export ban after Europe releases fuel reserves
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said Friday that the United States would not impose a diesel export ban, as he hailed a decision by European countries to release the fuel from their reserves. Trump added: "I asked for it. Trump had first said he backed a diesel export ban – which would have cut prices for US consumers but put pressure on supplies elsewhere around the world – on Sept 22.

items.title: Lethal injection, nitrogen, firing squads: How US states carry out executions
items.summary: THE unprecedented botched execution of a woman in Tennessee has reignited the debate over execution methods in the United States – which varies from lethal injection to firing squads. The condemned female murderer survived two lethal injections during a botched execution by the US state of Tennessee on Thursday. Lethal injection, authorised in 28 states and at the federal level, remains by far the most common execution method since the death penalty was reinstated in the United States in 1976.

items.title: Girl, 8, awarded RM12.19m in medical negligence suit
items.summary: MELAKA: The Ayer Keroh High Court today awarded RM12.19 million in damages to an 8-year-old girl in a medical negligence suit involving a government hospital and its doctors. Judicial Commissioner Datuk Isa Aziz Ibrahim awarded RM10.77 million in future general damages to cover the plaintiff's lifelong treatment, rehabilitation and multidisciplinary care. The girl was also awarded RM500,000 in general damages, RM441,754.83 in special damages, RM300,000 in aggravated damages, RM157,792.22 in pre-trial damages and RM176,718.75 in legal costs and expenses.

items.title: Four named suspects in deadly Java Sea ferry sinking
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian police have named four suspects in connection with the Virgo Transport 8 ferry that capsized and sank in the Java Sea on Sept 13. South Kalimantan police Sigit Haryono said the suspects were the ship's captain, an official from shipping and logistics company PT Virgo Karya Shipping, the company's branch manager and its operations manager. The ferry, carrying 243 people, departed Surabaya in East Java on Sept 12 for Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.

items.title: Nepal's nightmare and the case for climate accountability
items.summary: But a Nepali friend, a mountaineering guide, laments how the devastating Aug 26 glacial flood at the Nepal-Tibet border is having a dampening effect on the tourist trade impoverished Nepal heavily relies on. Life may be tough on the roof of the world, but climate change is making it infinitely worse. Nepal's plight brings into sharp focus not just the ill effects of climate change writ large, but also the corresponding issue of climate justice.

items.title: Trump holds sway over who wins Nobel Peace Prizes
items.summary: UNITED States President Donald Trump will not win this year's Nobel Peace Prize as he wages war with Iran, but his influence will still be felt by the awarding body that picks the laureate, according to experts. Last year's award, to Venezu-ela's Maria Corina Machado, was unique in the prize's 125-year history, coming amid repeated lobbying by Trump to get the award. "I think last year's events around the Nobel Peace Prize, Maria Corina Machado giving it to Trump afterwards, will affect some of the considerations that they make," he said.

items.title: NST Leader: Make Borneo postings feasible for doctors
items.summary: IT is that time of the year when newly appointed government medical doctors in the country report for work to their assigned hospitals or clinics. The Sabah Malaysian Medical Association chairman Dr Brandon Patrick Senagang was even quoted in the NST as saying the shortage of medical doctors in the state has reached a "breaking point". Of 138 medical officers from outside Sabah expected to report to their postings, he said, only a shocking 47 officers had done so.

items.title: Malaysia launches first multi-purpose mission ship in Türkiye
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's first Multi-Purpose Mission Ship (MPMS 1) for the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) has been launched in Istanbul, Türkiye, marking another milestone in maritime security cooperation between the two countries. The Home Ministry said the vessel was launched at Desan Shipyard today in a ceremony officiated by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. "The construction of MPMS 1 is a manifestation of the close relationship between Malaysia and the Republic of Türkiye, particularly in maritime security and enforcement," the ministry said.

items.title: 2027 school session to begin Jan 4
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 school session for national and government-aided schools will begin on Jan 4 and end on Dec 2 for Group A states and Dec 3 for Group B states. The Education Ministry (MoE) said Group A comprises Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, while Group B covers Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Perak, Perlis, Penang, Sabah, Sarawak, Selangor and the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya. MoE has also coordinated the festive holidays for the 2027 school session, covering Hari Raya Aidilfitri, Chinese New Year, Hari Raya Aidiladha, Kaamatan, Gawai Dayak, Wesak Day, Deepavali and Christmas.

items.title: 'Heavy plastic bag' turns out to be three mortar bombs
items.summary: SEPANG: A lorry driver who picked up a heavy package from a pile of rubbish in Sungai Balak, Kajang, was stunned to discover it contained three mortar bombs. Md Raduan Ghani, 41, said he had started work as usual around 4am on Friday, collecting and disposing of rubbish. Sepang police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report from the lorry driver around 3.30pm.

items.title: Rantau Panjang wants its buzz back — and traders hope ECRL is the answer
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 2 — Rantau Panjang was once a bustling border town, alive with the pulse of trade; however, the passage of time and a decline in visitor numbers have left some premises quiet, while the remaining traders continue to hope for a turnaround. The proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is seen not merely as a new transport option, but as a potential catalyst to revitalize economic activities in the town. Rantau Panjang resident Syed Abu Bakar Syed Daud, 65, who has lived in the area for over 50 years said he has personally witnessed the town's transformation, particularly regarding the number of visitors and traders.

items.title: Treat RM220m international maritime trade issue with same urgency as political cases, maritime expert tells MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan today questioned why an international maritime trade issue involving petroleum cargo worth more than RM220 million had yet to receive a clear answer from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), when the commission had moved swiftly on cases involving politicians. “Why is the MACC continuing to remain silent on this issue? Why does it appear that cases involving politicians are being given special attention, while an issue involving international maritime trade has yet to receive a clear answer?”

items.title: Coach Murad seeks clarity on who was behind threats against Caprice after police drop action against him
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — High-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Coach Murad or Murad Zaidi, wants to know who was behind an Instagram account that allegedly posted death threats against social media influencer Caprice and his family, after police decided to take no further action against him. “On July 11 last year, Murad Zaidi was arrested in connection with the investigation. “My client has consistently denied being behind the account and cooperated fully with the police investigation,” Aizzat said.

items.title: PM Anwar hails three more golds as Malaysia matches best-ever Asian Games haul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Malaysian athletes on winning three more gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan today, describing the achievement as a proud accomplishment that reflected their outstanding ability and determination. He said the latest haul brought Malaysia’s gold medal tally to nine as the national contingent continued its campaign to make the Jalur Gemilang proud on the Asian stage, matching Malaysia’s best-ever gold medal haul at the Asian Games, won at the 2010 Guangzhou edition. “Congratulations and well done to today’s gold medallists,” he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: No power struggles, says Selangor Sultan as current and former menteris besar meet
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today met and dined with two former Selangor menteris besar, Mohamad Khir Toyo and Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, as well as the current Menteri Besar, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. “This meeting reflects the Sultan of Selangor’s continuous concern regarding the state’s direction and the people’s livelihood, whilst demonstrating the good relationship between the royal institution and the state’s administrative leadership, including those who previously shouldered the responsibility,” according to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page. “His Royal Highness also reminded that Selangor’s progress must be accompanied by societal harmony and administrative stability.

items.title: Man detained after 230kg of subsidised cooking oil found hidden among rubbish at Melaka restaurant
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 2 — A Yemeni man in his 50s has been detained today for investigation into suspected unlawful possession of subsidised cooking oil at an Arab food restaurant in Bukit Baru here. Melaka Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director Dr Mohd Hazimin Jamaludin said 230 kilogrammes of packaged cooking oil worth RM575 were found during an Op Tiris 4.0 raid at the premises at about 1.30pm today. The subsidised cooking oil, comprising various brands, was found in several black plastic bags placed among a pile of dry waste, including old carpets, in a corner of the third floor of the premises, which had been converted into a workers’ dormitory.

items.title: Penang Free School marks 210 years with push for digital transformation
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 2 — Penang Free School (PFS), the oldest English-medium school in South-east Asia, is marking its 210th anniversary this year and is committed to strengthening its digital capabilities to better prepare students for the changing education and technology landscape. PFS Organising Committee chairman Ivan Ooi Jieun Vei said the anniversary celebrations also provided an opportunity to mobilise support for the PFS Digital Transformation Fund, aimed at enhancing the school’s digital infrastructure and capabilities. He said the fund focused on strengthening digital infrastructure, enhancing educators’ capabilities and exposing students to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, coding and new digital technologies.

items.title: HKL emergency dept upgrade enters final phase, completion targeted by end-2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The upgrading project of the new block of the Emergency and Trauma Department at the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) is now in the final phase of implementation. The HKL Management said today that several issues require repair and improvement work in the inspection and completion process before the facility can be fully completed. HKL said that it is committed to ensuring that all repair work is carried out properly to meet the facility’s safety, functional, and quality requirements before the project is finalised.

items.title: KL woman fined RM24,000 over fraudulent transfer of retiree’s RM1.1m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — An unemployed woman was fined RM24,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of fraudulently transferring RM1.1 million belonging to a retiree into her own bank account eight years ago. Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad imposed the fine on Chin Chew Woon, 43, and ordered her to serve 24 months’ imprisonment if she failed to settle the fine. According to the charges, Chin was accused of transferring RM500,000 and RM600,000 belonging to a 66-year-old man into her bank account in Brickfields on December 26 and 27, 2018.

items.title: JPJ suspends all MYEG Group services from Oct 5 over unresolved contractual obligations
items.summary: In a statement today, JPJ said the suspension covers My E.G. As a result, all JPJ services currently available through MYEG Group channels will be suspended from October 5. Vehicle ownership transfers can meanwhile be carried out through JPJ counters, selected kiosks, the JPJ public portal and eAuto for certain transactions.

items.title: RM5,000 trial payout leads Pontian victim into RM1.15m investment scam
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 2 — A private-sector employee lost RM1.15 million after falling victim to an online investment scam operated by a syndicate. Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said police received a report from the 52-year-old man yesterday, with preliminary investigations finding that the incident began in early January after he got acquainted with a woman via WhatsApp. “Convinced by the investment, the victim subsequently made several more transactions to several bank accounts in stages until March 26, 2026, involving a total of RM1,151,621.96,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: JB-Singapore RTS Link service start pushed back to February 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Passenger service on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is now expected to begin in February 2027, the Malaysian and Singaporean governments said today. In a joint statement, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Singapore Grantor) and the Ministry of Transport Malaysia (Malaysia Grantor) said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline. The new target is subject to RTSO obtaining independent safety certification for the RTS Link and securing final regulatory approvals.

items.title: Johor conservation efforts produce about 5,000 turtle hatchlings a year
items.summary: Johor Department of Fisheries director Rosmawati Ghazali said the main turtle nesting sites identified include Pulau Apil, Pulau Dayang, Pulau Besar and Pulau Tinggi here. However, Rosmawati said turtle eggs left to hatch naturally face a high risk of predation, so they transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries for closer monitoring. Therefore, we transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries so our personnel can monitor them more closely,” she said.

items.title: MCMC, MACC to use AI in fight against corruption and abuse of power
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will leverage artificial intelligence (AI) technology to detect, prevent and manage the risks of abuse of power and misappropriation more systematically and effectively. In a statement today, MCMC said this was among the areas of collaboration agreed upon by the two agencies through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen strategic cooperation in enforcement, corruption prevention and integrity empowerment in addressing complex challenges in the digital environment. The exchange of the MoU between MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din and MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman took place at the MCMC headquarters here today.

items.title: Department mobilises 153 firefighters, medevac teams and buses to ensure optimum safety during F1
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A total of 155 officers and members, along with 12 assets from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), have been deployed to ensure that the levels of safety, emergency preparedness, and rescue operations are at an optimum level throughout the hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026, scheduled to take place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). “The assignment of JBPM officers, personnel, and assets to strategic locations is to ensure that any emergency and rescue needs can be addressed quickly, orderly and effectively,” he said in a statement today. He said that 12 departmental assets are being mobilised throughout the event, comprising a Fire Rescue Tender, two Compact Fire Rescue Tenders, one 10,000-litre water tanker, three Emergency Medical Rescue Services ambulances and four JBPM buses.

items.title: Anwar secures fast-track process for missing Malaysians in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah has assured Malaysia of full cooperation to determine the status of 54 citizens still missing after devastating floods and landslides in Nepal, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He is willing to give all the cooperation,” Anwar said to reporters this afternoon, adding that Shah agreed during a bilateral call to facilitate administrative and legal efforts to help relatives obtain closure as quickly as possible. The standard legal procedures in Nepal typically require a three-year waiting period to issue a death certificate for missing persons, compared to six or seven years under Malaysian law, Anwar said.

items.title: Police arrest 13 in Teluk Intan raids, syndicate used Alipay accounts to move gambling proceeds
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Oct 2 — Police have arrested 13 people over a syndicate that allegedly used Alipay accounts opened with Malaysians’ passport details to receive and transfer proceeds from online gambling scams targeting Chinese nationals. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, comprising five Malaysians and eight Myanmar nationals aged between 20 and 44, were arrested in two raids here on Sept 28. Mohd Alwi said the syndicate, believed to have been operating since mid-July, had opened about 60 Alipay accounts using the personal details of local residents.

items.title: Court of Appeal overturns acquittal, jails ex‑bowling coach two more years for molesting 13‑year‑old
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A former bowling coach, already serving a prison term for sexual assault, was sentenced to an additional two years’ imprisonment by the Court of Appeal today for molesting another former Malaysia Games male athlete in 2017. A three-member bench led by Federal Court judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, sitting as a Court of Appeal judge, ordered Mat Salleh Jalani to begin serving the two-year sentence after completing his six-year prison term for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old male athlete in 2018. The court reinstated the Magistrates’ Court’s conviction and increased the sentence from 18 months to two years’ imprisonment.

items.title: Thunderstorms expected in KL, Selangor and nine states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 7pm today. In the weather advisory issued at 4pm, MetMalaysia indicated that the adverse weather will affect the entire northern states of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Perak, alongside the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Selangor, seven districts are on alert: Petaling, Sepang, Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Klang, Kuala Langat, and Gombak.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan urges BN to announce Melaka candidates early, give time to meet voters
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 2 — Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan has suggested that Barisan Nasional (BN) announce its candidate list for the Melaka state election early. Ahmad, who is also Umno War Room Secretariat chief, said an early announcement would give shortlisted candidates sufficient time to prepare and introduce themselves to voters. Ahmad, who is also Deputy Public Works Minister, said BN’s candidates for the Melaka state election would undergo three levels of screening before a final decision is made by the party’s top leadership.

items.title: KL Marathon goes ahead this weekend, but Kids Dash cancelled over haze concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – The Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 will proceed this weekend despite the haze, but organisers have cancelled the Kids Dash races to protect the health of young participants. In a race update, organisers said the Full Marathon, ASICS Half Marathon, IHH 10km and 5km will run as scheduled. “We regret to announce that the Kids Dash races will be cancelled, in the best interest of the children,” the organisers said.

items.title: State governments urged to gazette paddy land as rice self‑sufficiency drops to 54.3pc
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — State governments have been urged to gazette paddy-growing areas to sustain rice cultivation and strengthen the country’s food security after the rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) declined last year. According to the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM), the proposal was among the matters discussed at the second 2026 Agriculture and Food Security Ministers’ Meeting with state agriculture executive councillors, chaired by Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu yesterday. “Malaysia’s reliance on imported rice was estimated at 1.416 million metric tonnes, worth RM2.953 billion, in 2025,” KPKM said in a statement today.

items.title: MCMC probes AI‑manipulated footage of Dr Mahathir grieving wife’s death, warns of legal action
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has its eyes on social media content that allegedly uses artificial intelligence (AI) to manipulate footage of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad grieving the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. The commission said it had contacted the relevant social media platforms over the content. Suspected manipulated content should also be reported to the relevant platforms or authorities.
